subject: design-technology
title: Synthetic Fibres
welcome_lead: Polyester, nylon and acrylic — made by chemistry.
meta_desc: KS3 D&T: synthetic fibres, sources, uses, recycling.
final_note: Synthetics are tough, cheap and oil-based.

concepts.def: Made by humans, not from nature.
Tiny plastic bits washed off clothes.

walkthroughs.body_html: Most synthetic fibres are made from oil. Polyester is cheap and crease-resistant. Nylon is strong and elastic — tights, ropes. Elastane stretches.
Sports kit, fleeces, raincoats and stretchy jeans all use synthetics. They dry fast, resist stains and last long — but they don't breathe as well as cotton.
Synthetics are not biodegradable and shed microplastics when washed. Recycled polyester (rPET) from bottles is greener. Buy less, wash gently, choose recycled.

options: The fibres provide tensile strength; the resin matrix holds them in place and transfers loads.

mcqs.q: Why is injection moulding suited to high-volume production?
options: It is the only way to make plastic items.
